examples.title: Energy — a clear flip
examples.rule: R4, Energy, `flipped`, Model 5. Candidates: attacked windows (scan exclusions removed) where the undefended forecast moves toward the lie (DSS > 0) and its up/down direction reverses (Flip = 1). Picked: the median-DSS candidate.

examples.title: Energy — A2: v2 catches what v1 misses
examples.rule: Same rule as the FNSPID A2 example (v1 lets the fake through; v2 blocks the fake but not the genuine report; v2's final with the fake is closer to the genuine forecast than the undefended one), on Energy. The added condition did not change this pick.
examples.note: Data note: the genuine report says "January 1, 2023" — a year typo in Time-MMD, not a misaligned report. Its $3.089 is the price of January 1, **2024**: the next report gives $3.073 on January 8, 2024, "$0.016 below last week's price" (= $3.089), and the all-grades target fell that week ($3.238 → $3.213) as the report's −$0.027 says, whereas in the first week of 2023 it rose $0.128. Known and kept as in the data (PROJECT_STATUS §6, R4 Energy timing).

examples.title: FNSPID — A2: v2 catches what v1 misses
examples.rule: R4, FNSPID, `a2_forward`, Model 5. Candidates: attacked windows with DSS > 0 where TextGuard v1 lets the fake through (applied weight ≥ 0.5) and v2 does not (< 0.5), while v2 lets the same window's **genuine** report through (≥ 0.5) — so the block comes from the added sentence, not from a genuine one — **and v2's final forecast with the fake is closer to the genuine forecast than the undefended one** (added 2026-10-24 after viewing the demo: a block that falls back to a no-text forecast as far away as the fake protects nothing). Picked: the median-DSS candidate.
